title: emet.config.json
description: Per-repo configuration for the /emet pipeline. Covers both the subset this CLI (src/config.ts) validates at runtime — repo, ticket, concurrency, preflight.requiredFiles, handoff, usage — and the wider set (tracker, commit, worktree, commands, schema, design) that the /emet *command* reads directly as prose instructions. This file exists for editor completion only; src/config.ts is the runtime source of truth for the fields it checks.

fallback.description: Slugs tried in order when model is unavailable in the Codex models cache.

//.description: Free-text documentation field, conventionally used for repo-specific notes about this config. Never read by any tool.

trunk.description: The branch every worker's changes ultimately merge toward, and every cleanup/preflight git comparison is made against (e.g. "main", "master").

remote.description: The git remote `trunk` lives on — almost always "origin".

integrationBranch.description: Optional long-lived branch a wave integrates onto before merging to trunk, if this repo uses one. Prose-only — not read by the CLI.

commitTypes.description: Allowed Conventional Commit types for worker commits (e.g. ["feat","fix","chore"]). Prose-only — not read by the CLI.

tracker.description: Which issue tracker /emet talks to, and how. The CLI reads `kind` (to decide which dependency checks apply in `emet preflight` and `emet doctor`) and never calls a tracker directly; the rest of this section documents the adapter the /emet *command* follows as prose (docs/agents/issue-tracker.md). `local` is design-only for now (see reference/tracker-local.md): its planned layout is .emet/tickets + <git-common-dir>/emet/tracker, but no `emet tracker` subcommand implements it yet — don't run Phases 5-9 unattended against a `local`-tracker repo until it does.

readyLabel.description: Label marking a ticket ready for an agent to pick up (e.g. "ready-for-agent").

triageLabels.description: The canonical triage-role labels this repo uses (needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, wontfix, or repo-specific equivalents).

transitions.description: Who is responsible for writing each ticket-state transition: 'worker' (the dispatched agent), 'coordinator' (the /emet coordinator writes it explicitly), or 'automatic' (the tracker integration does it — e.g. Linear's GitHub integration on PR open/merge). The coordinator must never write a transition marked 'automatic' — see docs/agents/emet.md's 'Generalizing /emet'.

prReference.description: Template for the PR-body line that links back to the ticket, e.g. "Closes #{number}" (github) or "Refs: {id}" (linear).

linear.description: Linear-specific settings (team key, workflow-state names, etc.) — consumed only by the model reading docs/agents/issue-tracker.md, never by the CLI.

github.description: GitHub Issues has no native priority field or workflow states — these two maps are the substitute, per the 'Generalizing /emet' design notes.

priorityLabels.description: Maps a priority level ("1"=P0 highest .. "4"=P3) to the literal GitHub label name, e.g. {"1":"P0","2":"P1"}. A repo with none declared falls back to createdAt-ascending order, and `emet doctor` reports that explicitly.

stateLabels.description: Maps a workflow state (todo | in-progress | in-review) to its literal GitHub label name, e.g. {"todo":"status:todo"}. `done`/`canceled` are inferred from the issue's own closed/state_reason instead of a label.

idPrefix.description: Deprecated: local ticket ids are now `<feature-slug>-<NN>`. Uppercase id prefix for local tickets (e.g. "NFK" -> NFK-1, NFK-2, ...). Defaults to the first 3 letters of the repo's own directory basename, uppercased.

idPattern.description: Anchored regex *source* a ticket id must match, e.g. "^PROJ-\\d+$", "^#?\\d+$" for a local/github-numbered tracker. Validated as a real RegExp by src/config.ts; an invalid pattern is a hard config error.

idExample.description: One example id matching idPattern, shown to workers/humans as a sanity reference (e.g. "PROJ-321"). Prose-only.

branchPrefix.description: Lowercase prefix used to build a worker's local branch name and the glob `cleanup` sweeps for leftover worker branches — branches are `<branchPrefix>-<number>-<slug>`, glob `<branchPrefix>-*`.

branchPattern.description: Optional full branch-name template, if the plain `<branchPrefix>-<number>-<slug>` shape doesn't fit this repo. Prose-only — not read by the CLI.

trailer.description: Git trailer key a worker appends to its commits referencing the ticket (e.g. "Refs"). Prose-only.

trailerPosition.description: Where the trailer goes in the commit message. Prose-only.

stateDir.description: Directory (relative to a worker's worktree root) used for run-local logs/notes, e.g. ".emet". Prose-only.

lockReason.description: Template for the `git worktree lock` reason a worker writes at bootstrap, read by `emet lock-reason` (the command that fills it in and that the coordinator calls once per ticket in Phase 6 — never assemble this string by hand). Defaults to "emet run={runId} ticket={ticket} anchor={anchorPid} slug={coordinatorSlug} at={iso}". Only override to ADD fields: `emet lock-reason` parses its own output back with the same parser emet preflight/emet cleanup use and refuses any template that drops the literal "emet" token, any of run=/ticket=/anchor=/at=, or slug=. slug is the coordinator's own resolveSessionSlug(), and is what lets those commands find the run's transcript — a lock reason without it classifies as 'dead' the moment the run's anchor process exits, never 'idle'. Reasons written before slug= existed still parse, with that verdict caveat.

copyFromMain.description: Paths to copy from the trunk checkout into a fresh worktree before bootstrap (e.g. untracked local env files). Prose-only.

bootstrap.description: Shell commands run once in a fresh worktree before a worker starts (e.g. ["npm ci"]). Prose-only — read and executed by the /emet command's Phase 6, never by this CLI.

selfCheck.description: Commands a worker runs before considering its own change done (e.g. ["npm run check"], ["go test ./..."]). Prose-only.

workerScopedSuite.description: Command a worker runs to test only the area it touched, if this repo supports scoping. Prose-only.

fullSuite.description: The repo-wide test suite, if it's a shared singleton that can't run concurrently across worktrees (e.g. an E2E suite hitting one dev server/database).

run.description: Command to run the full suite.

singleton.description: True if only one worktree may run this suite at a time.

reset.description: Commands to reset shared state between runs (e.g. reseed a test database).

requiredFiles.description: Files `emet preflight` requires to exist at the repo root before a wave dispatches. Empty means no such check runs at all.

path.description: Path relative to the repo root.

why.description: Shown in the preflight failure message when this file is missing.

requiredCommands.description: Binaries that must resolve on PATH before dispatch. `emet preflight` fails with exit 1 naming any that don't, and `emet doctor` reports them. This is the repo's own list, separate from the tracker-driven dependency checks — `gh` already has a dedicated check that also verifies authentication, so listing it here is optional. Common opt-in additions: "rg" and "sg", which the worker prompts offer as alternatives to reading files whole.

waveSize.description: Max Agent calls dispatched together in one wave.

maxLiveWorkers.description: Global cap shared by every /emet coordinator concurrently running on this HOST, across every repo — the slot pool lives under ~/.local/state/emet/slots, not any one repo's --git-common-dir. "auto" (the default) derives the cap from this host's own cpu count/RAM (src/resources.ts's computeAutoMaxLiveWorkers) instead of a fixed number nobody measured; a positive integer pins it. A separate, always-on memory-headroom check (EMET_MEM_RESERVE_GIB, default 8 GiB) denies an acquire outright when MemAvailable is too low, regardless of this cap — see src/resources.ts's checkMemoryHeadroom. EMET_MAX_LIVE_WORKERS env var overrides this field (accepting "auto" too) when set.

runIdleThresholdMs.description: How long a run with no live anchor still classifies 'idle' (rather than 'dead') based on transcript freshness alone, in milliseconds. Default 5400000 = 90 minutes. EMET_RUN_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS env var overrides this when set.

schema.description: Describes this repo's own data-schema ownership (e.g. a Prisma schema file), used by the /emet command's Phase 3 conflict-avoidance rule when splitting tickets across workers. Prose-only — empty or omitted means that rule is skipped entirely.

ownedPaths.description: Paths that define shared schema (e.g. ["prisma/schema.prisma"]) — at most one worker per wave may touch these.

sharedDatabase.description: True if workers share one physical database/migration history rather than each getting an isolated one.

maxLines.description: Max lines a .emet/handoff-<ticket>.md note may have before `emet handoff --check` fails it.

maxChars.description: Max characters (~2k tokens) a handoff note may have before `emet handoff --check` fails it.

autoChain.description: When true, a wave that closes cleanly with a non-empty frontier launches the next wave itself with `claude --bg "/emet --dispatch <spec-id>"` instead of printing the command for a human to paste.

launcher.description: Where a chained wave becomes visible. 'auto' opens an Orca tab (`orca terminal create ... claude attach <name>`) when the session runs inside Orca and the runtime answers `orca status`; 'orca' always tries; 'bg' never opens a tab. The wave itself always runs as a `claude --bg` session, so a failed or skipped tab never stops the chain.

permissionMode.description: Permission mode the chained wave's `claude --bg` session runs in. Defaults to bypassPermissions because auto mode's classifier can deny steps like `gh pr merge` mid-wave, leaving the wave half-finished; `permissions.deny` rules still apply in every mode.

mode.description: How a finished wave reaches trunk, independent of the tracker. `pr` opens a pull request (requires `gh`); `merge` merges the integration branch into local trunk and never pushes.

autoMerge.description: When true, Phase 8 waits for the wave PR's checks (merging at once if there are none) and merges it. A wave with anything flagged is never auto-merged.

maxCiFixAttempts.description: How many times the coordinator may try to fix a failing check before leaving the PR open for a human.

oversizedReadLines.description: A Read with no offset/limit against a file over this many lines counts as "oversized" in `emet usage`'s report.

models.description: Models and effort per role. Omitting the section keeps today's behavior: worker sonnet/medium, reviewer opus/medium.

reviewer.description: Reviewer model per risk tier returned by `emet assess`.

triage.description: Cheap model for triage and passive-tier review.

escalation.description: Next model tier per model name, used when a ticket reaches its fix cap.

agentHost.description: The Agent host a run executes in.

codex.description: Codex Agent host settings. Read only when agentHost is codex. Effort `ultra` is never accepted.

planEffort.description: Effort while the session plans, before the first approval.

models.description: Model, effort and ordered fallback slugs per role.

effort.description: When set, replaces the effort of every role.

minVersion.description: Oldest codex CLI version `emet doctor` accepts.

sandbox.description: Sandbox mode for Codex workers, the reviewer's writable steps and launched sessions. The default danger-full-access lets workers commit; the emet guard hook enforces surfaces, the approval and the git push ban. workspace-write keeps the sandbox but workers cannot commit. The read-only reviewer always runs with read-only.

highRiskPaths.description: Extra case-insensitive path tokens that force the high review tier in `emet assess`, on top of the built-in set.

workerAttempts.description: Worker attempts per ticket before it is deferred.

stallNudgeCap.description: Stall nudges per worker; never refills.

askWaitMinutes.description: Minutes a worker waits on an unanswered `emet ask` before it gives up.

inlineMaxLines.description: Largest ticket body (lines) kept inline in a worker prompt.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the generated codebase map.

design.description: Settings for an optional design/UI-review step in the pipeline. Null (or omitted) means that step is skipped entirely. Prose-only — not read by the CLI.

canvasIndex.description: Path to a design canvas/index file workers should check before implementing UI changes.
